sources.files: Every sound file is mono, true peak at most -1 dBTP; credits in the wiki's Sound-Credits page. The open-sea beds and the surf are mastered toward -8 LUFS (each records what it reached), events (knocks, cracks, break-ups, snapping lashings, a breaker's slam, water over the gunwale, slaps) to -18 LUFS with a limiter, and the rest of the ambience (lapping, slosh, leak, whitecaps) to -26 LUFS. A volume can't exceed 1, so a file's master is the loudest it can play.
sources.levels: Volumes set against vanilla by calculation from its code: in the game a sound plays at its file's loudness + 20 log10(volume x the player's setting for its type x distance attenuation). Distance attenuation is OpenAL exponent-clamped with reference max(3, sqrt(range) - 2) and rolloff ln 100 / ln range; weather and our beds play relative to the listener, unattenuated. Vanilla at sea: wind -39 LUFS just audible, -31 at wind speed 0.7, -24 in a full gale; rain -33 moderate, -27 heavy; raft idle -50; shore lapping -51 beside 100 edge blocks.
sources.beds: Over sea water with waves of at least seaFromMetres (a pond or a creek in a gale stays quiet), by the wind speed at the listener in m/s, not the wave height: a young sea in a gale already roars. lufs is the sea's level in the game, -46 + 30 log10(wind / 2 m/s): -46 at 2 m/s, -34 at 5, -20 at 15 (past vanilla's full wind at -24), -12 at force 10, -9.3 from 35 m/s, the loudest the storm's file can play; each loop's lufs is its file's measured loudness, mastered toward -8. A storm deafens: events stay at their own level (a hard knock -18) and drown in it from about force 8.
sources.shore: Block ambient, volume clamp(sqrt(blocks) / surfBlockCount) x strength x the band's gain. Surf files are mastered toward -8 LUFS and reached -10.6 to -15.5; each band's gain brings its file to the loudest (-10.6), so the level runs smoothly across bands. Strength grows with the wave height at the shore as the sea's bed grows with the wind: beside 500 breaking blocks -44 LUFS in 0.3 m waves, -32 at 1 m, -24 at 2 m, -16 at 3.5 m, -13 from 5 m, so a storm coast roars as loud as the storm at sea. Lapping replaces vanilla's waterwaves (-36.75 LUFS) with a -26 LUFS file at 0.29 x the strength vanilla's would need.
sources.hull: At a rider 1.5 m away: slap -40 to -32, full bilge slosh -34, leak trickle at most -40, hull lapping -44. The whitecap hiss -37 LUFS at 12 m, under a force-6 wind.
sources.events: An event plays at least 6 dB over the loudest background of the moment, the full gale's wind at -24 LUFS: a hard knock, a crack, a break-up and a slam at -18, a light knock at -24, water over the gunwale -26 to -19. The reed boat's soft crunches only reach -24 under the limiter.
sources.vanillaRowingVolume: Scales vanilla's own rowing sound (raft-moving, -26 LUFS at full speed, unpositioned) to -40, under our beds, keeping it as the sound of the oars.
